author: claude
review_correction: The claimed 'no MTP' boundary is false for the pinned t6040-j614s-dcuart.dtb (SHA-256 30b01736b5291aaa864f37f73192ec9877da97ab8ecf5d72c1ca92cf9c8af05d): DT decompilation shows the DockChannel HID ASC mailbox, DART, DockChannel mailbox, and hid@514600000 all status=okay. The live console confirms dockchannel-hid RTKit/MTP initialization and input attachment. This run can exclude PCIe/ANS/SMC DMA, but it cannot exclude MTP/DockChannel-HID DMA or support the ticket's broad 'CPU/MMU is fine' / 'drivers exonerated' conclusions. A true no-MTP follow-up needs a distinct reviewed DTB while retaining ttydc0.
desc: 205 discriminator: is the bulk-store corruption a CPU/MMU problem at all, or a DMA-capable coprocessor writing into RAM Linux believes is free? Every 205 boot so far has run the FULL driver set -- PCIe, brcmfmac (WLAN DMA), hci_bcm4377, nvme-apple/ANS (RTKit + SART DMA), MTP (dockchannel HID, RTKit DMA), SMC, SD/sdhci -- all of which DMA into kernel memory, and several of which are RTKit coprocessors whose shared-memory regions m1n1 sets up. If one of them writes outside its mapping, a bulk store into a freshly allocated page is exactly what would fault or corrupt, it would scale with system activity (hence with core count), and it would be hidden by tiny delays. TEST: boot the THIN DTB t6040-j614s-dcuart.dtb (dockchannel UART only -- no PCIe, no ANS, no MTP, no SMC) with the RAM-root initramfs-dcuart.cpio.gz (the SD root cannot be used: it needs PCIe for the card) at maxcpus=14, then run scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh >=4 times with a fresh-boot baseline. BOOTS CLEAN => the CPU/MMU is fine and a driver/coprocessor DMA is the culprit; bisect by re-enabling subsystems one at a time (PCIe, then ANS, then MTP). HANGS => drivers are exonerated and it is genuinely CPU/MMU/coherency, which also means the reproducer works without any of our peripheral bring-up and gets much simpler. Per ticket 208/218 method rules: re-measure the control in the SAME session and image, and never conclude from one run. RESULT 2026-08-03 -- BREAKTHROUGH: SMC IS THE CULPRIT. At maxcpus=14, same kernel and same initramfs-dcuart RAM root, only the DTB varying: thin dcuart = 14 CPUs boot (447 lines); dcuart-pcie = 14 CPUs boot (496) so PCIe EXONERATED; wifi minus ANS/NVMe = HANG so ANS EXONERATED; wifi MINUS SMC = 14 CPUs boot (458) => SMC IS THE CULPRIT; full wifi = hang; control full DTB + the SAME RAM root = hang, so the initramfs is not the variable. Disabling smc + smc_mbox alone takes maxcpus=14 from 100% hang to all 14 cores up. This reframes 205 entirely: never a CPU/MMU/cache/TLB bug -- macsmc disturbs memory as core count rises, and the five bulk-store signatures on freshly allocated pages are the SYMPTOM. Explains why any perturbation hid it, why five unrelated callers faulted, why severity scaled with cores, and why round 8s config knobs looked effective. CANNOT just disable SMC: it provides the gP13/gP19 pwren-gpios that power WiFi/BT/SD plus RTC and battery. NEXT: (1) disable only the smc_gpio child; (2) drop macsmc-hwmon/power/rtc consumers selectively; (3) PRIME SUSPECT -- verify the SMC RTKit shared-memory/SRAM window (our reg is smc + sram; a wrong sram size would let SMC write outside what Linux reserved); (4) this is very likely the "weird crashes with smp" yuka/sven discussed on 08-02, and "depends on the kernel config" fits WHICH SMC CONSUMERS are built in. ROUND 10b 2026-08-03: (1) SRAM-SIZE HYPOTHESIS REFUTED. Shrinking sram to 16 KiB or 32 KiB does let 14 CPUs boot, but only because SMC then FAILS to initialise ("Failed to initialize shared memory (-14)") -- the failing buffer offset TRACKS the declared size (16K->0x6000, 32K->0x8000) because RTKit keeps requesting more buffers as earlier ones succeed. So the real region is larger than either, 1 MiB stays the best value, and the window has been RESTORED with the refutation written into the DT comment. Shrinking sram is not a fix, just another way to disable SMC. (2) CPUFREQ REFUTED: SMC enabled with cpufreq absent (wifi.dtb) still hangs at 14 cores, so power/thermal via DVFS is out. (3) UNTESTED ASSUMPTION worth flagging: the 14-core failure is a hang with ZERO kernel console output (dies before console registers, i.e. likely macsmc PROBE), while the 5-6 core failure is the intermittent bulk-store corruption -- these may be TWO different bugs and I have not shown they are one. NEXT: (a) disable only the smc_gpio child; (b) drop SENSORS_MACSMC_HWMON/MACSMC_POWER/RTC_DRV_MACSMC/POWER_RESET_MACSMC selectively; (c) if those are inconclusive, build DOCKCHANNEL_EARLYCON to get ANY output from the 14-core pre-console death -- currently it is pass/fail with no diagnosis. ROUND 11 2026-08-03 -- PINNED. Single-variable bisect at maxcpus=14: full wifi DTB = hang; wifi-nosmc = 14 CPUs; smc-nogpio (SMC RTKit alive, no gpiochip, no pwren) = 14 CPUs (509); smc-gpio-nopwren (SMC alive, gpiochip REGISTERS, pwren-gpios REMOVED) = 14 CPUs (510). So the trigger is specifically the gP13/gP19 SMC KEY WRITES that pcie-apple performs via gpiod_set_value() during port probe. Everything else about SMC survives 14 cores: RTKit initialises, macsmc-reboot binds, gpio-macsmc registers its gpiochip. Two key writes, once each, early in boot. NOTE this fits the 14-core symptom being a PRE-CONSOLE death, distinct from the 5-6 core intermittent bulk-store faults -- likely two separate problems. KEY PRIOR EVIDENCE now load-bearing: sol decoded 2026-07-29 that macOS writes gP13 <- 0x00800001 while gpio-macsmc writes CMD_OUTPUT|1 = 0x01000001; also the ADT has a function-pcie_port_control = PrtC(0x57) step and a 100 ms wlan_reg_on_on_delay we never implemented. NEXT: (1) write macOS value 0x00800001 instead and retest at 14 -- would give mechanism AND fix; (2) add the 100 ms delay / do the write before secondary bringup, to separate wrong-value from wrong-timing; (3) drop pwren from port01 (SD) only, keeping port00 (WiFi) -- if gP13 alone is safe we could ship WiFi at full core count immediately; (4) DOCKCHANNEL_EARLYCON so the hang stops being pass/fail. ROUND 12 CORRECTION 2026-08-03: (a) macOS GPIO value 0x00800001 tested at 14 cores -- STILL HANGS, hypothesis REFUTED, patch reverted. (b) ROUND 11 HAD A CONFOUND: removing pwren-gpios also prevents the PCIe endpoints powering, so brcmfmac/hci_bcm4377/sdhci-pci never probe and never DMA. Verified by counting pwren-gpios per DTB: every 14-core-booting DTB has 0, the hanging one has 2. The claim "SMC key writes are the trigger" is DOWNGRADED to "something in the chain SMC-write -> endpoint-power -> driver-probe -> endpoint-DMA breaks it". Separating experiment is ticket 223.
